I found two likely bugs in `src/accelerate/utils/fsdp_utils.py`. I only read the code and ran no tests.

1. **Line 693: the upcast breaks RAM-efficient loading.** The new block runs before the `cpu_ram_efficient_loading` move to `meta`, and `original_sd = model.state_dict()` (line 648) is taken earlier still.
   - `param.data = param.data.to(torch.float32)` builds a full fp32 copy of every trainable param on every rank, including non-main ranks.
   - On rank 0 the old low-precision `original_sd` tensors stay alive too, so it holds both copies.
   - That adds a large transient CPU RAM spike, which is the thing `cpu_ram_efficient_loading` exists to avoid.
   - It would be safer to upcast after the model is on `meta`, or to upcast the shards when they load.
   - `fsdp2_load_full_state_dict` casts `full_sd` to the model's current dtype (fp32 after the upcast). So the loaded values still have only bf16 precision, and fp32 master weights get no extra precision from the checkpoint.

2. **Line 693: only `requires_grad` params are upcast, so the model can still have mixed dtypes.** Frozen params, for example the base weights under LoRA, stay bf16 while trainable ones become fp32.
   - If FSDP2 needs a uniform dtype across the params in a group, which is what the new comment says, that group is still non-uniform.
   - The new tests use a model where every param is trainable, so they don't cover this.
   - The previous code also filtered on `requires_grad`, so this may be intended. It is still worth checking against how FSDP2 treats frozen params.

The old upcast was effectively a no-op because `param = param.to(...)` only rebound the local name. That means this change makes memory use go up for any bf16 or fp16 model, since all trainable weights are now stored in fp32. The warning text already says so.

The new test cases and the `**{extra_arg: dtype}` cleanup in `tests/fsdp/test_fsdp.py` look correct.
